title: Affine-base structure on the Proj of an invertible section ring
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme and $f:X\to S$ a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], and let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $A=\Gamma_*(X,L)$ with its graded commutative ring structure [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. The degree-zero coefficient map $c:\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\to A_0$ places a function in the zeroth direct summand through the canonical identification $L^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_X$; it preserves zero, one, addition and multiplication, and is regarded as a ring homomorphism. Define the affine-base structure map $p:\operatorname{Proj}(A)\to S$ [def-pc-proj] to be the composite of $\operatorname{Proj}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A_0)$, $\operatorname{Spec}(c\circ f^\#):\operatorname{Spec}(A_0)\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$, and the inverse of the canonical affine isomorphism $S\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$. If all positive-power section nonvanishing opens cover $X$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], denote by $r:X\to\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ the normalized canonical morphism of [lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map], with its prescribed inverse-image and fraction formulas. This definition uses those formulas to specify $r$ uniquely; it imposes no ampleness hypothesis.
